julgamento-pareado.d: An evaluation in which both models answer the same prompt and a judge picks the better response (or a tie). Since the prompt's difficulty affects both sides, it cancels out in the duel.

intervalo-de-wilson.d: An analytic confidence interval for a proportion, better than the normal approximation for small \(n\) or \(p\) near 0 or 1: it pulls the center toward 0.5 with \(z^2/n\) terms and never leaves [0, 1].

vies-de-verbosidade.d: The tendency of judges (humans and LLMs) and of reward models to reward longer, more formatted answers. Swapping positions doesn't fix it; it takes length control (WR-LC) or style control.

painel-de-juizes.d: Several smaller judges from disjoint families with a majority vote, in place of one large judge. PoLL (Verga et al., 2024) showed less intra-model bias and was more than 7× cheaper. In Module 1, GLM, Qwen and DeepSeek form a homemade panel.

controle-de-estilo.d: Bradley–Terry regression with style covariates (length, headers, lists, bold): \(\operatorname{logit}P(i\succ j) = s_i - s_j + \gamma^\top(f_i - f_j)\). The ranking publishes the strengths \(s\), that is, who would win with the same style. The default on LMArena since 2025.

chatbot-arena.d: A platform of anonymous battles between two models with human votes; the ranking is a Bradley–Terry fit with style control, reported on an Elo-like scale. The methodology is open in the arena-rank package.

maldicao-do-vencedor.d: Selection bias: when you measure several variants with noise and publish the top-scoring one, you publish the luckiest one. The expected maximum grows with the number of variants, even if they are all equal. It's one of the mechanisms behind the “Leaderboard Illusion.”

conjunto-de-selecao.d: The split between the data used to choose checkpoints and hyperparameters (selection) and the data looked at only once to report the result (reporting). It prevents selection contamination and the winner's curse.

alpacaeval.d: A benchmark of 805 instructions judged against the gpt4_turbo baseline by a GPT-4 Turbo annotator; it costs less than US$10. The LC version controls for length and raised the Spearman correlation with Chatbot Arena from 0.94 to 0.98.

wr-lc.d: The counterfactual win rate at equal length: fit a logistic regression of the verdict on the length difference (\(\tanh(\Delta\ell/\sigma)\)) and read the prediction at \(\Delta\ell = 0\), \(\mathrm{WR}_{LC} = 100\,\sigma(\theta)\).

arena-hard.d: A benchmark of hard prompts distilled from Chatbot Arena and judged by an LLM. v0.1: 500 prompts, 3× more separation than MT-Bench, 98.6% correlation with human rankings. v2.0: 750 prompts (500 + 250 creative writing), style control with --control-features.

mt-bench.d: 80 two-turn questions in 8 categories, scored 1 to 10 by a strong judge. Saturated in 2026, but useful for detecting multi-turn regression.

ifeval.d: A benchmark of 25 types of code-verifiable instructions (word counts, JSON, no commas…) in ~500 prompts (541 rows in the dataset). Prompt-level and instruction-level metrics, strict and loose. A cheap detector of an SFT that broke formatting.

aime.d: An American math competition with 30 problems per year (I + II). With so few items, each question is worth 3.3 pp: report pass@1 averaged over several samples. Use the most recent exams (2026), because the older ones show signs of contamination.

pass-at-k.d: The probability that at least one of k attempts is correct; unbiased estimator with n samples and c correct: \(1 - \binom{n-c}{k}/\binom{n}{k}\) (Chen et al., 2021). It measures capability: “does it ever work?”

pass-hat-k.d: The probability that all k attempts are correct: \(\binom{c}{k}/\binom{n}{k}\) (Yao et al., 2024, τ-bench). It measures agent reliability: “does it always work?” It falls with k; pass^1 = pass@1.

swe-bench.d: A benchmark of fixing real issues in Python repositories, verified by tests. Verified (500) was abandoned by OpenAI in 2026 over defective tests and leakage (secondary source); Pro and Pro Verified are the successors.

bfcl.d: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard: non-live, enterprise/OSS, multi-turn and agentic web-search function calls (V4, April 2026). The overall score is the unweighted average of the subcategories.

tau2-bench.d: An agent benchmark in simulated customer service, with a user simulator and tools on both sides (airline, retail, telecom, banking_knowledge domains…). It reports pass^k to measure reliability.

mcnemar.d: A paired test for per-item binary metrics: only the discordant items count, \(\chi^2 = (|b-c|-1)^2/(b+c)\), with \(b\) = right on the base and wrong on the candidate and \(c\) = the opposite. It detects regressions that unpaired CIs hide.

lm-eval-harness.d: EleutherAI's tool for running standardized benchmarks (IFEval, GSM8K, AIME, HumanEval, MMLU-Pro…). It points at an OpenAI-compatible server (local-chat-completions for generative tasks, local-completions for log-likelihood) or uses vLLM directly, LoRA adapters included.

contaminacao.d: Leakage of evaluation items into training (pretraining, synthetic data from a teacher that memorized them) or into decisions (choosing a checkpoint by looking at the test). The score ends up measuring memory, not capability.

descontaminacao-ngramas.d: Removing from training every item that shares a normalized n-gram (usually 8 to 13 words) with any evaluation set. It catches near-copies, but not paraphrases.

min-k-prob.d: A contamination detector (Shi et al.): the mean log-prob of a text's K% least likely tokens. Texts seen in training have fewer “surprise words,” so the score is higher (less negative).

sonda-de-recusa.d: A cheap diagnostic for safety regression: project the residual activations of harmful and harmless prompts onto the refusal direction estimated on the base and compare the separation before and after the fine-tune (an inference from Arditi et al.).

ancora-kl.d: The \(-\beta\,\mathrm{KL}(\pi\|\pi_{\text{ref}})\) term in the RLHF/DPO objective, which ties the policy to the reference. The realized KL is the budget spent by post-training; it is estimated per sample with \(k_3 = (\rho - 1) - \log\rho\).
